title: Materials
tagline: Where every item goes and what reads it: house chests, camp stock, ship holds and saddle slots, and the materials each one needs.
asOf: Current to Charting the Unknown · patches through 2.05.01 · November 2026

metrics.label: Capacity
metrics.blurb: How much it holds, in slots, at the most it can reach. Tier I is 1,000 or more; II 240 to 999; III 50 to 239; IV 10 to 49; V under 10.

metrics.label: Payoff
metrics.blurb: What it does beyond holding. Tier I feeds a mechanic straight from storage or removes a chore across the game; III is storage only; V is cosmetic or one-off.

metrics.label: Unlock
metrics.blurb: What it takes to have it. Tier I is there now or one stop away; Tier V is late DLC work or a fortune.

rules.text: A slot holds one stack: 50 ore, 20 hay, but a single fish or insect. Rated on the most it can reach, so the Kuku Cooler rates on 1,000 stacked, not the quest cooler's 40.

rules.lead: Payoff is what it does beyond holding.
rules.text: Read in place by crafting, cooking, trade or the camp ranks highest; plain storage rates III.
Capacity isn't rated for supplies, or for stores whose size no source publishes: Camp Provisions, wagons and Island Storage.
Every manifest is ranked against every other, house, ship and mount alike.

ladderNote: Tiers rank each manifest against every other, on what it holds, what it does and what it takes.

leaves.label: House Storage
leaves.short: The house chests, the camp's stock and chest, and the Kuku Pot.
leaves.blurb: The places at home that hold items: the 1.04 house chests that crafting and cooking read, Private Storage, Carl's stock and Supply Chest, and the Kuku Pot. Each manifest lists what belongs in it, by name.

leaves.label: Ship Storage
leaves.short: Holds, shipbuilding stock, fittings, hidden blueprints and sea materials.
leaves.blurb: Everything a ship stores and needs: its hold, the camp stock a build draws on, the outfitters' parts, the blueprints hidden at sea, the materials only the ocean gives, and island storage.

leaves.label: Mount Storage
leaves.short: Trade slots, wagon cargo, feed and the materials mount gear takes.
leaves.blurb: What mounts carry and what they consume: a horse's trade slots, a wagon's cargo, feed, the craftable horse tack, and the Kuku line's mount gear.

route.title: Set-up Order
route.blurb: When each store opens through the story, and what to put in it the moment it does.
route.premise: A new character with a 50-slot bag. Each phase opens with the chapter that unlocks it; the Sorter says where every item goes once it does.

phases.label: The first chest
phases.why: Patch 1.00.03 put Private Storage in reach before the camp: dump spare gear and materials there instead of selling them, and buy the 50-copper Small Bags as you pass vendors.

steps.text: Use the chest in the north-east tent of the Freesword Encampment, then the one at the Hernand lodgings.
Buy a Small Bag (+1 slot, 50 copper) at every vendor; take quests that pay Medium Bags.

phases.label: The house and the camp
phases.why: The camp and the Hernand Residence open together. Buy a Sturdy Gatherables Chest first: from then on the Smithy reads your materials at home.

steps.text: Buy one for 50 Silver at the Timberham Sawmill furniture shop and place it in Build Mode; move ore, timber, hides and herbs in.
Private Storage now lives in Kliff's tent at camp.
After the Reed Devil, donate spare gear, ore, timber and food to Carl: missions spend it.
Empty Carl's Supply Chest each visit; it stops collecting at 230.

phases.label: The pot and the cooler
phases.why: Mysterious Pot hands you the Kuku Pot, and A Special Blueprint turns one into a cooler that cooking reads.

steps.text: Seal Abyss objects and machine parts as you find them; Grimnir's recipes use them.
Craft the Kuku Cooler at Grimnir's: a Kuku Pot, 5 Iron Ore, 3 Copper Ore and 1 Azurite. Move ingredients, fish and feed in.

phases.label: Paper, outfits and tack
phases.why: Quest paper and outfits are the next slot hogs, and both have chests. Pick up the horse tack blueprint and a wagon on the way.

steps.text: Early Encounter gives the Collectibles Chest: quest items, keys, notes and recipes.
Buy Wardrobes in Timberton, Delesyia (15 Silver): outfits for all three, worn from the housing screen.
Thornbriar Fortress holds the Wells Military tack blueprint.
Brice's Request builds your trading wagon.

phases.label: Grow it all to 1,000
phases.why: Camp expansions take Private Storage to 1,000, and late research opens the Enhanced cooler and Blackstar's armour.

steps.text: Each of the first four expansions adds 100 slots; the fifth adds 360.
The Enhanced Kuku Cooler (330) needs Mercury from Delesyia research after Chapter XI, plus Brimstone, Rubber and Electrical Components.
After the move to Pailune, Private Storage becomes an item you can place in the house.
After Chapter XI, an empty Kuku Pot becomes the part for Blackstar's armour.

phases.label: Holds and islands
phases.why: Ships bring new stores and a new class of materials. Stock Carl before the first build; the best parts are hidden, not sold.

steps.text: Donate 600 Stone, 600 Wood and 1,200 Food to Carl, then start Small Shipbuilding.
Trade goods ride in the hold: 6 to 36 slots by hull.
Fit the Ship Teleportation Device so the ship becomes a fast-travel point.
Hunt the four hidden ship blueprints.
Collect Shiny Ore, deposits, Ambergris and pearls as you sail.
Build Island Storage on a pioneered island.
